pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
# Introduction

Welcome to the API documentation. This guide provides everything you need to integrate with our platform.

## Getting Started

To begin using the API, you'll need to create an account and obtain your API key. All requests must be authenticated using a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

```
Authorization: Bearer your-api-key-here
```

## Base URL

All API endpoints are relative to the following base URL:

```
https://api.example.com/v1
```

## Content Type

All requests and responses use JSON format. Ensure you set the `Content-Type` header to `application/json`.

pages.title: Authentication
pages.content:
# Authentication

Our API uses API keys for authentication. You can manage your API keys from the dashboard.

## How to Authenticate

Include your API key in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token:

```http
GET /v1/users
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc123def456
```

## API Key Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `sk_live_*` | Production API keys |
| `sk_test_*` | Test API keys |

## Rate Limiting

API requests are rate-limited to 100 requests per minute per key. If you exceed this limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

pages.title: Users
pages.content:
# Users

The Users API allows you to manage user accounts in your application.

## List Users

```http
GET /users
```

Returns a paginated list of users.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| `page`    | number | Page number |
| `limit`   | number | Items per page |

### Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "usr_123",
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "total": 42,
  "page": 1
}
```

## Create User

```http
POST /users
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "John Doe",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "password": "securepassword"
}
```

pages.title: Products
pages.content:
# Products

Manage your product catalog through the Products API.

## List Products

```http
GET /products
```

Returns all products with optional filtering.

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| `category` | string | Filter by category |
| `search`  | string | Search by name |

## Create Product

```http
POST /products
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "Premium Plan",
  "price": 29.99,
  "description": "Our best-selling plan",
  "category": "subscription"
}
```

## Update Product

```http
PUT /products/:id
```

Partially update a product's information.

pages.title: Orders
pages.content:
# Orders

The Orders API handles order processing and management.

## Create Order

```http
POST /orders
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "user_id": "usr_123",
  "items": [
    {
      "product_id": "prod_456",
      "quantity": 2
    }
  ],
  "shipping_address": {
    "street": "123 Main St",
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "state": "CA",
    "zip": "94105"
  }
}
```

## List Orders

```http
GET /orders
```

Returns all orders for the authenticated user.

## Get Order

```http
GET /orders/:id
```

Returns detailed information about a specific order, including line items and status.

pages.title: Error Handling
pages.content:
# Error Handling

Our API returns consistent error responses to help you debug issues quickly.

## Error Format

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "message": "The request was invalid",
    "details": {
      "field": "email",
      "reason": "Invalid email format"
    }
  }
}
```

## HTTP Status Codes

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `200` | Success |
| `201` | Created |
| `400` | Bad Request |
| `401` | Unauthorized |
| `404` | Not Found |
| `429` | Rate Limited |
| `500` | Internal Server Error |

## Common Errors

- **invalid_request**: The request body is malformed or missing required fields.
- **unauthorized**: The API key is missing or invalid.
- **not_found**: The requested resource does not exist.
- **rate_limited**: You've exceeded the rate limit.

pages.title: Webhooks
pages.content:
# Webhooks

Webhooks allow you to receive real-time notifications about events in your account.

## Setup

Configure your webhook endpoint URL in the dashboard. We'll send POST requests to your endpoint when events occur.

## Event Types

| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `order.created` | A new order was placed |
| `order.updated` | An order status changed |
| `payment.succeeded` | A payment was successful |
| `payment.failed` | A payment failed |
| `user.created` | A new user registered |

## Signature Verification

Each webhook request includes a signature header that you should verify:

```
X-Webhook-Signature: t=1234567890,s=abc123def456
```

Verify the signature using your webhook secret to ensure the request is legitimate.

## Retry Policy

If your endpoint returns a non-2xx response, we'll retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff.

pages.title: SDKs & Libraries
pages.content:
# SDKs & Libraries

We provide official SDKs for popular programming languages.

## JavaScript / TypeScript

```bash
npm install @example/api-client
```

```javascript
import ExampleAPI from '@example/api-client';

const client = new ExampleAPI('sk_live_abc123');
const users = await client.users.list();
```

## Python

```bash
pip install example-api
```

```python
from example_api import Client

client = Client('sk_live_abc123')
users = client.users.list()
```

## Go

```bash
go get github.com/example/api-go
```

```go
import "github.com/example/api-go"

client := api.NewClient("sk_live_abc123")
users, err := client.Users.List()
```

## 🚧 Community SDKs

Community-maintained SDKs are available for Ruby, PHP, Java, and .NET. These are not officially supported by our team.
